extracted.intended_audience: federal agency information resource managers, STI program managers, IRM/CIO offices, and policy implementers responsible for Scientific and Technical Information (STI)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for managing scientific and technical information (STI) within federal agencies, covering planning, systems lifecycle, acquisition, dissemination, data quality, interoperability, security, and cost/accountability. Intended to help agencies implement OMB Circular A-130 requirements for STI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work process redesign and IT to improve STI operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Is your agency carrying out any work process redesign or application of information technology to improve effectiveness and efficiency of STI operations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether agencies are actively redesigning processes or applying IT specifically to improve STI operations; look for documented initiatives and expected efficiency/effectiveness gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life-cycle benefit-cost analyses for information systems supporting STI
rubrics_metrics.description: Does your agency have life-cycle benefit-cost analyses done for each information system supporting STI?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider: level of detail relative to investment size and how responsibility is determined; consistency with OMB A-94 guidelines; reliance on systematic measures of mission performance (effectiveness of program delivery, efficiency of program administration, reduction in burden on the public); whether analyses are undertaken for major systems agency-wide as part of ongoing management oversight; description of processes used; existence of post-implementation reviews to validate benefits, document effective management practices, and convey lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic IRM planning that includes STI
rubrics_metrics.description: Does your agency have a strategic information resources management planning process that includes STI?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether planning addresses how management of information resources promotes agency mission fulfillment and whether STI is explicitly included in the IRM plan; check that STI coverage anticipates changes in mission, policy, technology capability, or resource levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of STI in planning and budgeting for public information collection burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Is STI included in the planning and budgeting for the information collection burden imposed on the public as defined by 5 CFR 1320?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify STI-related collections are incorporated into Office of Management and Budget/agency information collection planning and that burden estimates and budgets reflect STI activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational IT planning linked to STI and five-year planning requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Is operational information technology planning linked to anticipated STI and mission needs, and are STI needs reflected in the up-to-date, five-year plan as required by 44 U.S.C. 3506?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that existing and planned major information systems for STI are reflected in the plan; planned IT acquisitions for STI are included; major systems and acquisitions support the STI mission; STI requirements are included in computer security planning; and planning is coordinated with strategic, human resources, and financial planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review to ensure systems meet mission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there agency periodic review of information systems supporting STI to determine if mission requirements have changed and whether systems continue to fulfill and anticipate mission requirements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether reviews determine required maintenance levels to keep systems cost-effective and aligned to mission, and whether the agency documents results and follows up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability for lifecycle management of STI systems
rubrics_metrics.description: How does the agency ensure that the official responsible for administering an STI program supported by an information system is responsible and accountable for management of that system throughout its life cycle?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for clear assignment of responsibility and accountability for system management from planning through disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for users of Federal information resources supporting STI
rubrics_metrics.description: What training is provided for the users of Federal information resources that support STI?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate user training programs for adequacy in enabling effective use of STI systems and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of state/local/tribal prerogatives regarding STI systems
rubrics_metrics.description: How are the prerogatives of State, local, and tribal governments vis-à-vis systems supporting STI protected from undue restrictions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess policies and procedures that safeguard the authorities and access of subnational partners when STI systems affect them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinated resource decisionmaking and IRM governance
rubrics_metrics.description: How is decisionmaking about information, human, financial, and other supporting resources coordinated so that systems proceed in a timely fashion toward milestones in the life cycle and deliver intended benefits?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether there is an agency-wide management or IRM committee, whether STI is represented, and whether coordination mechanisms ensure timely progress to deliver benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial management conformance for STI
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the financial management system supporting STI in conformance with OMB Circular A-127?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify STI financial systems follow OMB A-127 requirements for federal financial management and controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management and technical framework linking mission, content, and IT
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe your agency’s management and technical framework for using information resources that document linkages between STI mission needs, information content, and information technology capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the framework parameters (e.g., technical standards) and how linkages are documented and managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperability, portability, and scalability of STI systems
rubrics_metrics.description: How does your agency ensure that information systems supporting STI are developed in a manner that facilitates necessary interoperability, application portability, and scalability of computerized application across networks of heterogeneous components?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess design standards, architecture decisions, and procurement practices that promote interoperability, portability, and scalability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of duplicative information systems development
rubrics_metrics.description: How does the agency ensure that unnecessarily duplicative information systems development is avoided?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider duplication from within the agency, with other agencies, and with the private sector; review mechanisms to identify and prevent duplication and promote reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms for intra- and interagency sharing of STI systems
rubrics_metrics.description: What mechanisms are in place to share available information systems supporting STI with other agencies, and how are sharing opportunities identified?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for documented sharing agreements, discovery of sharing opportunities, and evidence that sharing is occurring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost accounting and equitable cost recovery for shared services
rubrics_metrics.description: Do any STI organizations manage Information Processing Service Organizations? If so, do you account for full costs of operation and recover costs from all service recipients on an equitable basis?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine cost-accounting practices, recovery mechanisms, and documentation of sharing agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security level establishment for STI information systems
rubrics_metrics.description: How is the security level established for information systems supporting STI? Are levels commensurate with the risk and harm that could result from loss, misuse, or unauthorized access or modification to information in the systems?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate risk assessments, classification/impact analyses, and alignment of security controls to potential harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of full and open competition for IT acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Does your agency use full and open competition for acquisition of information technology?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm procurement practices favor competition unless exceptions are justified and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for off-the-shelf software and justification for custom development
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it agency policy to use off-the-shelf software? Are methods of justification clear to develop custom software?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess acquisition policies that favor commercial solutions and require clear, documented justification for custom development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures to ensure conformance to OMB Circular A-109
rubrics_metrics.description: Are procedures in place to ensure conformance to OMB Circular A-109?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify procurement and acquisition procedures align with OMB A-109 guidance on major information systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of individuals with disabilities in IT acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: How are individuals with disabilities needs taken into consideration in the acquisition of information technology?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for accessibility requirements, procurement language, and testing to ensure IT meets needs of individuals with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life-cycle information management policy for STI-funded programs (DOE example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departmental policy that programs funding the creation of scientific and technical information must follow life-cycle information management practices to ensure information is planned for, budgeted, produced, processed, disseminated, and stored in cost-effective ways to ensure its maximum utilization by all customer segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a model policy: require life-cycle management in program funding decisions; ensure consideration of production, dissemination, storage, and customer access needs and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic planning as a living document with resources and oversight (NLM example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic/long-range planning should be a living document that includes an executive summary, detailed recommendations, panel deliberations, discrete recommendations tied to staff and budget resources, and mechanisms to track progress and incorporate updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure plans drive budgets, allow tracking of progress year-to-year, provide channels to acquire external expertise for topics not on staff, and accommodate emerging opportunities (e.g., outreach, digital libraries, training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive information management strategic plan (EMAP example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an information management strategic plan presenting a vision, high-level user requirements, guiding principles, a technical approach, a project management approach, and a high-level implementation plan; coordinate with other agency planning and subject the plan to rigorous peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer review and stakeholder coordination; involve representative communities in design and pilot testing; solicit feedback through customer surveys and other mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggressive, modern information collection strategies (DTIC/EDMS example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt aggressive information collection strategies that include nontraditional sources and formats, evaluate commercial document delivery services, handle copyrighted information, and transition from paper-based to electronic collection and EDMS capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capabilities should include scanning to electronic images, storage on optical/media, acceptance of electronic inputs (disk/CD-ROM/Internet), full-text retrieval, and electronic cataloging/abstracting/indexing without requiring the physical document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality management components for scientific data (EMAP QMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure scientific data integrity through Accountability, Usefulness, and Inherent Quality: (1) Accountability — assign responsibility and document adherence to schedules and protocols; (2) Usefulness — define data purpose and set Data Quality Objectives (DQOs) and Measurement Quality Objectives (MQOs); (3) Inherent Quality — use appropriate scientifically based laboratory practices, quality control, and acceptable sampling/analytical techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement QMP and project-specific QAPPs, perform peer reviews and quality assurance reviews, conduct Data Quality Assessments for intended uses, and provide access to methods metadata, data pedigree, and QA reports to support traceability and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and standardization in international collection and exchange (OSTI example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote international agreements and standard exchange formats (e.g., SGML) and use Internet receipt mechanisms to improve timeliness and availability of STI (OSTI provides >90% of received international information to DOE community within three days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor multilateral agreements that share processing costs and standardize exchange formats to reduce effort and improve timeliness; adopt electronic receipt channels to speed availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible, multi-platform dissemination and user interfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide dissemination via multiple media (Web, CD-ROM, email, gopher, ftp), support a range of platforms (Windows, Macintosh, UNIX), and deploy user-friendly interfaces (graphical UIs, assisted/expert query screens) with help/tutorials to make STI accessible to both experienced and inexperienced users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement search services (e.g., WAIS, DGIS), consistent command languages or GUIs (e.g., GoldenGate), help features and tutorials, and appropriate registration for unclassified services while maximizing public access where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and multiple access methods (NAL example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use optical scanning and OCR to produce CD-ROMs and other preservation media, support electronic document delivery and interlibrary borrowing, and ensure multiple means of access based on users' capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan preservation programs that balance depth of access and durability; provide alternative access channels (offline, dial-up, Internet) so users without Internet access can still obtain materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to national/international standards to facilitate access
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to bibliographic cataloging standards, information interchange standards, and participate in international efforts (e.g., unified thesaurus) to reconcile vocabularies and improve worldwide access to subject literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support standardization efforts (cataloging, interchange formats, thesauri) to reduce integration costs and improve interoperability across institutions and countries.
